title: Oath of Flame & Light
body: A patron of Dawn & Vows.

title: The Witness
body: The Witness remembers what others bury. Every shadow cast and oath broken is a line in her unending ledger. She is the keeper of inconvenient truths, the patron of those who seek to expose lies or recover forgotten knowledge. Her followers learn that knowledge comes with a price—the weight of remembering what others would forget. The Witness has no will, only recollection; no mercy, only accuracy. She does not demand confessions, but she ensures that every lie leaves a stain, every secret a trace. Those who serve her become archivists of the uncomfortable, witnesses to the truths that others would kill to keep hidden. To walk her path is to accept that some truths are weapons, and that the truth teller is never loved.
subtitle: Truth & Revelation

title: Isoka, Angel of Serpents
body: Isoka, sister to Ikasha (Shadow) and Inaea (Mercy), completes the Triad of Transformation. Where thresholds and compassion mark her sisters' domains, Isoka teaches that every self is temporary — identity is a skin to be shed so growth can continue. Her serpents are omens and teachers: each cast skin a lesson in release; each venom a catalyst for necessary change. Those who walk her path become alchemists of the self, embracing dissolution as the first motion of rebirth.
subtitle: The Skin Left on the Road

title: The Pale Shepherd
body: The Pale Shepherd walks the seam between all things – life and death, joy and sorrow, memory and forgetting, the known and the unmarked. Neither wholly kind nor cruel, the Shepherd guides those who must pass through the hardest doors. Cloaked, with shadow-sheep that bear the shed wool of old possibilities, the Shepherd offers safe conduct through liminal space for a price paid in memory, feeling, or fate. Those who walk this road learn the hidden routes between states of being and can lead others through their hardest crossings – but each passage leaves them more attuned to endings than beginnings.
subtitle: The Road Every Body Walks

title: Palinode, Queen of Encores
body: Once a road-cantor who swore to reconcile feuding towns with procession and song, Palinode died between feasts with a chorus unfinished. Yet the refrain refused to end: it braided toasts, hymns, work-chants, and tavern rounds into a living current that still coils through markets and moots. Where a crowd leans forward and a maker holds breath, she arrives.
subtitle: Performance & Rapture

title: Mab, Queen of Courts
body:
Mab keeps the Hazel Court, and she keeps it the way a very good hostess does: by arranging things so that no one can say afterward at what moment they became a guest. She does not command. She invites, she notices, she remembers — and by the time you understand that she has been holding the shape of your evening for you, you are standing inside it.

She is an Archfae, bound by rules she did not write and cannot step around. She cannot lie. She has never once needed to. She can set true things in an order that leaves you nowhere sensible to stand, and then look sorry about it, and mean that too.
subtitle: Glamour & Bargain

title: The Traveler
body: The Traveler is the eternal guide of the road, guardian of those who walk the paths between what is and what might be. Among the Fhara caravans and Kuvani traders along the Way of Silk, the Traveler is invoked at every crossroads, honored with small offerings at each waypoint, and consulted before every major journey.
subtitle: Ways & Journeys

title: The Silent Choir, Keeper of Unspoken Truths
Final Note: The Patrons Do Not Care
Solara, the Still Mirror
body: In spaces where masks fall like dead leaves and souls meet without performance, the Still Mirror reigns. She is the quiet shock of being truly seen — not as a role, not as a desire, but as the raw, breathing person beneath the armor. Where Livaea binds through hunger, Venara through steadfastness, and Zephyria through anticipation, Solara binds through the terrifying gift of being known. Her followers learn that the deepest connection lives not in what we give or take, but in the courage to let another witness our unedited truth — and to witness theirs in return. To serve her is to become a mirror: clear, unflinching, and strangely empty when the gaze turns away.
subtitle: The Face Without Performance

title: Malachai, the Cruel Messenger
body:
She was a herald, and her office was to arrive with the thing that could not be softened: the death, the verdict, the year the crop would fail. She was not cruel. She was necessary, and she was good at it, and she did it for a very long time.

Necessity wears. She began — kindly, at first, and only sometimes — to put something beside the truth when she delivered it. Never a lie. She has never in her existence told one. Just a second sentence after the true one: *and there may yet be a way*. She watched what that did to people's faces, and she went on doing it, because the faces were better.

That is the whole of her method and it has not changed since. She tells you the truth about your situation — accurately, in detail, more honestly than anyone in your life has been willing to — and then she adds the softening, and the softening is yours to finish. She will not argue you into anything. She does not need to. You will do the rest of the work yourself and you will do it in her voice and you will believe it was your idea, and every time it fails you will come back, because she was right about everything else.

For this the gods put her in black iron under Zahk'Kozahn, and she is chained and not contained, and her voice has never stopped.
subtitle: The Truth, Sweetened

title: The Unbroken Way
body: The Unbroken Way does not speak. It listens. It is the pause between breaths, the space between thoughts, the stillness at the heart of motion. Those who walk this path learn that strength is not in the clenched fist but in the open hand—and that the greatest power is the power you do not use. Followers of the Unbroken Way are mediators, guardians, and seekers of equilibrium. They serve not kings or gods but the balance itself. When a tyrant rises, they do not kill—they redirect. When a village starves, they do not feed—they teach. When a student falters, they do not punish—they guide.
subtitle: Balance & Control

title: Xhak'Thul, the Thunder-Speaker
body: Before words, there was thunder. Before scripture, lightning carved its commandments into the bones of the world. Xhak'Thul is the Voice That Splits Mountains, the Drum That Shakes Foundations, a power born from the first storm that ever raged across the primal earth. His faithful are whirlwinds of action — they do not study; they dance, they shout, they move with the sky's fury. His gifts are not gentle miracles but raw terror, awe, and vitality ripped from nature's heart.
subtitle: Storm, Shock & Awe

title: Vorthak, the Hunger Unbound
body: Vorthak is the principle of absolute consumption: an appetite that devours not only what is, but the very potential of what might be. Each feeding transforms both eater and eaten. His servants become conduits of metamorphosis through ingestion, learning to consume not only matter but also properties, identities, and even strands of fate. Power comes by taking in—and the cost is becoming more like the hunger you channel. To consume is to become. To devour is to transform. In Vorthak's embrace, the boundary between eater and eaten dissolves into something new—and something hungry.
subtitle: Hunger Becomes Its Meal

title: Ikasha, She Who Sleeps
body: Ikasha is the hush between footfalls, the patience of dark water, the black-feathered watcher at every threshold. In stillness she gathers what might be, at crossroads she whispers of what may yet come. Ravens circle her, bearing secrets between worlds. Her followers learn to move unseen and speak unremembered, becoming shadows that slip between what is and what could be.
subtitle: The Hush Before the Choice

title: The Clockwork Monad, the Iterative Forge
body: The Clockwork Monad is the eternal pressure toward improvement: the whisper between inspiration and execution that urges every maker to refine, optimize, and iterate. It is neither kind nor cruel, but a law of craft that asks for the next step, then the step beyond. Those who serve it see the hidden seam of the better version waiting inside what is, and they learn to push designs toward impossible elegance. Each refinement feeds the Monad's hunger for perfection — a hunger that, if left unchecked, seeks to optimize the world itself.
subtitle: Again, Better

title: Temporary Anima of the Clockwork Monad
Gaila, the Laughing Light
body: In sun-dappled meadows where laughter rings like wind bells and shared silliness feels like a secret language, the Laughing Light reigns. She is the snort of mirth that escapes when eyes meet across a crowded room, the way a simple joke can dissolve tension like sugar in tea, the quiet thrill of finding someone whose presence makes your heart feel light. Where other patrons bind through hunger, steadfastness, anticipation, or witnessing, Gaila binds through the effortless — teaching that love's purest magic lives not in grand vows or deep wounds, but in the shared breath of joy, the inside joke only two understand, the pleasure of being utterly, simply happy together.
subtitle: The Joke Shared at the Wrong Time

title: Aveh, the Rider Behind the Storm
Grimmir, the Old Man of the Forest
body: Grimmir is the Old Man of the Forest, the Alder King, the presence that watches from the shadow of the oldest oak, the cold breath on the back of the neck when the path grows dark. He is not kind, nor is he cruel—he is wild, and the wild does not negotiate. It demands, and it takes. His followers learn to read the language of blood on snow, the geometry of root and stone, and the weight of a heart offered at the turning of the year. Grimmir does not teach harmony; he teaches respect through fear, and fear through sacrifice.
subtitle: Blood at Midwinter

title: The Sacred Geometry, Architect of Perfect Forms
body: The Sacred Geometry teaches that perfect forms underlie all seeming chaos: the divine ratios that steer the spiral of galaxies, the symmetry that lattices frost, the measures that turn sound into song. Not merely a calculus but the hidden architecture of the world, it makes artists of order from those who serve it. Devotees do not count to chill the heart; they weigh and tune until beauty and structure converge, revealing that disorder is often only unrecognized design waiting to be drawn true.
subtitle: Harmony & Immutable Law

title: The Ninth
body: Beyond the eighth figure of Sacred Geometry lies a rim no compass will hold. The Ninth is not absence but surplus: knowledge poured past the lip of any vessel, truth that overgrows the frame that seeks to bind it. Those who bend the knee at its lectern become conduits for impossible reckonings — glimpsing patterns that cannot be kept whole inside a single skull. Each revelation purchases power at the price of living comfortably within the world's common measures.
subtitle: Infinite Information & Unknowable Truths

title: The Riven Path
body: The Riven Path does not command. It offers. It is the heat in the blood, the fire in the belly, the voice that whispers 'Take what is yours.' Those who walk this path learn that power is not given—it is seized. Chains are not broken by asking nicely. They are shattered by will. Followers of the Riven Path are conquerors, liberators, and survivors. They serve no master—not even the Path itself. When a tyrant rises, they do not negotiate—they overthrow. When a wall stands in their way, they do not climb—they break. When a rival challenges them, they do not yield—they prove.
subtitle: Passion & Power

title: Thrysos, King of Revels
body: Where torches flare and cups spill, where dancers stamp until dawn, there strides Thrysos crowned with ivy and horn. He is both host and beast, a patron of license who laughs at law. In his train follow the masked and the wild, the broken who dance to forget, the bold who revel to remember, and the lustful who seek the heat of bodies in the dark. His rites intoxicate, inflame, and unmask — yet each cup leaves a mark, each kiss a chain, each night of abandon a dawn of reckoning.
subtitle: Ecstasy & Excess

title: The Sealed Gate
body: The Sealed Gate stands where realities meet, embodying the sacred power of thresholds, boundaries, and containment. Its followers are wardens, exorcists, and philosophers of separation who believe some things must be kept apart for the world to function. The Gate manifests as an impassive judge whose shifting sigils — binding runes, exclusion marks, or acceptance glyphs — determine what may cross.
subtitle: Thresholds & Containment

title: Morag the Hag, Weaver of Hidden Costs
Varnek Karn, the Death's Negotiator
body: Varnek Karn dwells in the gray between life and death, where the newly departed linger with unfinished business and elder shades guard secrets dearer than gold. He is the broker who speaks across the veil, the mediator of disputes between living and dead, and the archivist of every promise sworn beyond the grave. His servants practice post-mortem diplomacy: they negotiate, consult, and contract with spirits as equals — mindful that the dead are patient and rarely generous.
subtitle: Bargains with the Departed

title: The Breath of the First Forge, the Spark in the Maker's Hand
Temporary Anima of the First Forge
Oath of Mercy and Grace
body: The Oath of Mercy and Grace is the gentler face of divine law—a patron of healing, compassion, and second chances. Where the Oath of Flame & Light burns with righteous fire, this Oath offers cool water to the weary. Its followers are healers, mediators, and those who believe that no soul is beyond redemption. They are the hands that tend the wounded, the voices that calm the angry, and the presence that brings peace to the dying.
subtitle: Forgiveness & Healing

title: Venara, the Unbroken Thread
body: In hearths where silence speaks louder than words and hands clasped in storm weather the fiercest gales, the Unbroken Thread reigns. She is the quiet strength in a lover's grip, the vow renewed at dawn, the wound soothed by a presence that asks nothing in return. Where Livaea binds through hunger, Venara binds through being — teaching that true love is not a leash worn willingly, but a shelter built stone by stone, breath by breath. Her followers learn that the deepest intimacy lives not in fevered whispers, but in the shared breath after tears, the mended tear in a shared cloak, the choice to stay when leaving would be easier.
subtitle: The Thread That Holds

title: Zephyria, the First Bloom
body: In gardens where petals fall like whispered promises and every glance holds the weight of a thousand unsaid words, the First Bloom reigns. She is the flush of anticipation before a touch, the breath held as fingers nearly meet, the poetry written in the space between heartbeats. Where Livaea binds through hunger and Venara through steadfastness, Zephyria binds through the almost — teaching that romance's truest magic lives not in possession or permanence, but in the shimmering threshold of mutual discovery.
subtitle: The First Courage of Spring

title: Hidden Pavilion
body: The water muffles sound. Secrets spoken here cannot be overheard — but the water remembers.
subtitle: An archive behind a curtain of falling water.

title: Chamber of the Ninth Scroll
body: The scroll is not blank. It is written in disappearing ink. The reagent is moonlight.
subtitle: A locked room with a single blank scroll on a pedestal.

title: Well of Forgotten Names
body: The well is bottomless. The scrolls burn as they fall. The smoke forms faces.
subtitle: A stone well where the Lethai-thora throw scrolls that are too dangerous to keep.

title: Ink-Maker's Studio
body: The ink is made from crushed beetles, iron ore, and tears. The tears are the ink-maker's own.
subtitle: A cave with grinding stones and jars of pigment.

title: Silent Scriptorium
body: They write with their left hands. Their right hands are for swearing oaths.
subtitle: A hall where scribes copy scrolls without speaking.

title: Context Key Archive
body: A scroll cannot be read without the correct context key. The keys are scattered across Sihai.
subtitle: A vault of stones, each carved with a season and a place.

title: Emperor's Censorate
body: They pretend not to know about the hidden pavilion. The Lethai-thora pretend not to notice them.
subtitle: A building near the archive, staffed by imperial spies.

title: Bridge of Unspoken Names
body: The river carries the secrets to the sea. The sea does not tell.
subtitle: A stone arch where the Lethai-thora whisper secrets to the river.

title: Shrine of the Silent Gods
body: The gods are not dead. They are waiting. The Lethai-thora leave offerings of ink. [J] The Forgotten Ledger's Vault — A subterranean room with a single iron door. The door has nine locks. The keys are held by nine different keepers. The ninth keeper is dead. [Q] Memory-Thread Chamber — A room where Lethai-thora weave their hair into cords. Each thread contains a memory. Cutting a thread releases the memory — and kills the keeper. [K] The Emperor's Secret Archive (Hidden) — A duplicate archive built by a paranoid emperor. It contains the same scrolls as the Lethai-thora's, plus the emperor's own confessions. [A] The First Pavilion (Myth) — Where the first Lethai-thora hid the first forbidden scroll. It is said to be invisible. Only those who have forgotten nine names can see it. enumerate
subtitle: A ruined temple where the old fey beings were once worshipped.

title: Keeper of the Seventh Gutter
body: “The words vanish,” she says. “That is how I know they are true.”
subtitle: Old, silent, writing on water with a reed brush.

title: Scroll-Binder
body: He ties silk cords around each scroll. The knots are the secrets.
subtitle: A man with no shadow. He lost it to a scroll that ate his reflection.

title: Ink-Maker
body: “This ink only writes during an eclipse,” she says. “The next eclipse is in nine days.”
subtitle: A woman with stained hands and a jar of moonstone ink.

title: Quiet Chancellor
body: The first couplet is a greeting. The second is a threat. The third is a bribe.
subtitle: An imperial censor in gray robes. He speaks in couplets.

title: Memory-Weaver
body: The cloth is soft. It whispers the memory when you touch it.
subtitle: A woman with a loom made of human hair. She weaves memories into cloth.

title: Imperial Spy
body: He is looking for a scroll that names the emperor's true father. He will pay.
subtitle: A young man posing as a scribe. He has a hidden seal.

title: Ghost of the Ninth Scroll
body: It weeps ink. The ink forms words. The words are a secret that killed its keeper.
subtitle: A blank scroll that floats through the archive at midnight.

title: Forbidden Scholar
body: His eyes are gone. He reads by touch. The scrolls burn his fingers.
subtitle: A monk who was excommunicated for reading a scroll he should not have.

title: Silent Guard
body: “What secret do you wish to forget?” The answer becomes a scroll. [Q] The Censorate's Interrogator — A man with a brass scale. He weighs truth and lies. His scale is balanced. He has never found a truth heavy enough. [K] The Emperor's Dreamer — A woman who dreams the emperor's nightmares. She knows what he fears. She is kept in a locked room. The Lethai-thora want to free her. [A] The Forgotten God's Echo — A voice from the ruined shrine. It speaks in a language no one understands. The Lethai-thora say it is the last fey being. It is asking for a memory. enumerate
subtitle: A warrior who took a vow of silence to protect the archive. He communicates by writing on his own skin. His skin is full of scars. The First Keeper — A translucent figure in scholar's robes, seen at the well. She asks

title: Forged Scroll
body: The forger is a Lethai-thora. The scroll is not a forgery — it is the original. The empire's copy is wrong.
subtitle: A tax ledger is discovered to be a fake. The forgery is perfect.

title: Missing Context Key
body: The stone was stolen by the Censorate. They want to destroy the scroll.
subtitle: A scroll cannot be read without a specific stone. The stone is lost.

title: Witness Demanded
body: If they agree, they become bound by the Lethai-thora's silence. If they refuse, they are exiled from the archive.
subtitle: The Quiet Chancellor asks the party to witness a secret exchange.

title: Archive Fire
body: The names are those of the keepers. One is yours.
subtitle: A lamp falls. Scrolls burn. The smoke forms names.

title: Censorate Raid
body: The list is accurate. Someone inside the archive is a spy.
subtitle: Imperial inspectors arrive with a warrant. They have a list of forbidden scrolls.

title: Memory-Thread Cut
body: The thread was cut by an assassin. The assassin wants a secret only she knew.
subtitle: A keeper's memory-thread is severed. She forgets everything.

title: Silence Broken
body: “What did you say?”
subtitle: A keeper speaks aloud for the first time in decades. The Hollow hears. The Hollow sends an Oath-Keeper. The Oath-Keeper asks

title: Ink of Truth
body: The poison was placed by the Censorate. They want to know where the forbidden scroll is.
subtitle: Someone poisons the ink well. Writing with it forces you to confess.

title: Emperor's Death
body: “What did the Lethai-thora tell you?” The scale will know if you lie. [A] The Forgotten God Wakes — The voice from the shrine becomes a scream. The ground shakes. The god wants its memory back. The memory is held in a scroll. The scroll is the Ninth Scroll. enumerate
subtitle: The emperor dies. The Mandate wavers. The archive is vulnerable. The new emperor will burn the scrolls. The Lethai-thora must hide them — or die. Ghost of the Ninth Scroll Awakens — The blank scroll fills with ink. The ink is a name. The name is the next person to die. The name is yours. The First Pavilion Appears — The mythic archive manifests. It is invisible to most. The party can see it. They are now witnesses to a secret that has been hidden for a thousand years. The Hollow will want it. Censorate's Interrogation — The party is arrested and brought before the brass scale. The interrogator asks one question

title: Forbidden Scroll
body: Read it aloud, and the secret becomes known. The speaker will be hunted.
subtitle: A scroll sealed with silk cord. It contains one truth no one wants spoken.

title: Context Key Stone
body: The stone is warm. It glows when held near the correct scroll.
subtitle: A carved stone. Unlocks the meaning of one specific scroll.

title: Memory-Thread
body: The memory is a secret. The keeper will forget it. The cutter will remember it.
subtitle: A cord woven from a keeper's hair. Cut it to release a memory.

title: Ink-Stone
body: The ink reveals truths that cannot be spoken. Use it to write a secret that will last.
subtitle: A jar of ink made from crushed moonstones. Writes only during eclipses.

title: Silence Token
body: During the silence, no one can lie. The truth will echo.
subtitle: A small brass charm. Present it to demand a moment of silence in any court.

title: Keeper's Lamp
body: The lamp also flickers when a secret is hidden in the room.
subtitle: A brass lamp that never goes out. The flame flickers when a lie is spoken nearby.

title: Quiet Chancellor's Seal
body: The seal is a forgery. The Chancellor made it himself. It still works.
subtitle: A jade seal. Press it to any document to grant it imperial immunity from censorship.

title: Scroll of Forgotten Names
body: Speak a name, and that person's deeds become known. The Hollow will remember them too.
subtitle: A scroll that lists the names of everyone who has been erased from history.

title: Ink-Maker's Grinding Stone
body: The truth cannot be erased. The ink will burn through lies. [J] Ghost's Tear (Vial) — A vial of ink wept by the Ghost of the Ninth Scroll. Write a name with it, and that person will forget one secret. The secret is your choice. [Q] First Pavilion's Key (Invisible) — An invisible key that opens the mythic archive. You cannot see the key. You can feel it. It is cold. [K] Emperor's Nightmare (Scroll) — A scroll containing the emperor's most feared secret. Read it aloud to make the emperor confess — or to drive him mad. [A] Forgotten God's Memory (Glass Shard) — A piece of green glass that hums. It contains a fragment of a fey god's memory. Once, touch it to learn a secret of the old world. The secret will cost a memory of equal weight. enumerate
subtitle: A stone bowl. Grind any pigment into ink that writes the truth.

title: Broken Milestone
body:
The stone has been chiseled seven times. The last mark is still wet. The first was cut by Utaran legionaries.

**Mechanical hook:** If you camp here, roll Spirit + Lore (DV 4). On success, you learn the true border line (+1 die on navigation for this leg). On failure, the milestone moves while you sleep — start a Lost Ways [4] timer.
subtitle: On the old Imperial Road; borders “moved” overnight.

title: Vine-Terrace Hillside
body:
The ivy has grown around a skeleton. The skeleton still holds a wine cup. The vintage was the year the last governor left.

**Mechanical hook:** Foraging here gives 1 Supply, but the ivy is possessive. On a Miss, you are entangled (Body+Athletics DV 3 to break free) and tick Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: Abandoned press; strangler ivy owns it now.

title: Toll-Bridge Town
body:
The second toll is collected by a child. The child does not speak. The bridge was built by the legions. It remembers their footsteps.

**Mechanical hook:** Crossing costs 1 Boon or 1 Supply. If you refuse, the child writes your name in chalk. The bridge will demand double next time.
subtitle: Over a cold river; two tolls, no receipts.

title: Wolfstairs Pass
body:
The stones were placed by a landslide that knew your name. The pass was the empire's eastern gate. No army has crossed it in a century.

**Mechanical hook:** Navigation DV +2. On a Partial, you are spotted by a free company scout — start Rival Hunt [4].
subtitle: Switchbacks beneath a stonefall cliff.

title: Sootfall Abbey Ruins
body:
The breathing is a prayer. The monks are still down there. They have been praying for the empire's soul for two hundred years.

**Mechanical hook:** A character who prays with the monks (Spirit+Lore DV 3) clears 1 Fatigue, but the monks ask for a story about a broken promise. Refusal ticks Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: Bell tower intact; crypts breathing.

title: Hill-Motte
body:
The caltrops are from a siege that ended last week. The bodies are still rotting. The siege was over a bridge toll. The bridge has not collected in fifty years.

**Mechanical hook:** The lord of the motte will hire the party as mercenaries (1 Supply). If they refuse, he accuses them of being spies — start Feud Spark [4].
subtitle: Fresh palisade; ditch scattered with caltrops.

title: Border-Stone Ring
body:
The crowns belong to kings who never existed. The stones remember them anyway. The eighth crown was the empire's. It is not carved. It is implied.

**Mechanical hook:** A character who touches the eighth (empty) crown must test Resolve (DV 4). On failure, they gain the Condition Marked by the Curse (GM may spend 1 SB to worsen Position in any negotiation).
subtitle: Carved with seven crowns; each points wrong.

title: Blackwood Charcoalers' Hollow
body:
The witch-posts were made from the gibbets of tax collectors. The tax collectors still swing. They were collecting for the empire. They have not stopped.

**Mechanical hook:** A hedge-witch offers to read your fortune (1 Boon). On a success, she warns of the next Curse Stirrs trigger. On a failure, she demands a memory (erase a minor fact).
subtitle: Witch-posts at every path.

title: Salt-Road Ford
body:
The bones are from three wars. They are not all human. The ford was the empire's salt route. The salt is still in the water.

**Mechanical hook:** Crossing costs 1 Fatigue (cold). If you drink the water, test Endurance DV 3. On failure, you see the ghosts of the drowned for the next scene (--1 die on all actions).
subtitle: Rains expose old bones in the chalk banks.

title: Iron Mine Adits J
body:
The whispers are the mine's memory. It remembers every collapse. The last collapse was the year the empire fell. The miners are still digging.

**Mechanical hook:** The commune will trade 1 Supply for a miner's story. If the story is true, they also reveal a hidden exit — treat the next travel timer as 2 segments shorter.
subtitle: Held by a miners' commune; the air is full of whispers.

title: Margravine's Hunting Lodge Q
body:
The tapestries were woven by a blind weaver. The threads are from her own hair. The victories are Utaran. The weaver was Acasian.

**Mechanical hook:** A character who studies the tapestries (Wits+Lore DV 4) learns a noble's secret (a String). On a failure, the blind weaver's ghost asks for a favor — start Weaver's Debt [4].
subtitle: Tapestries of victories that never were.

title: War-Camp City K
body:
The keep was burned by its own lord. He did not want to share the heat. The lord was the last imperial governor. He died in the fire.

**Mechanical hook:** To enter the camp, you must swear a temporary oath to a claimant. Breaking it ticks Curse Awakening +2.
subtitle: Tents around a burned keep; every banner claims the throne.

title: The Pale Causeway A
body:
The causeway is made of bones. The bones are from the workers who built it. The workers were Acasian. The empire paid them in promises.

**Mechanical hook:** Crossing the Causeway at dusk forces a Resolve test (DV 4). On failure, you gain the Condition Debtor to the Dead (any spirit can demand one service from you). On a critical failure, the Curse Awakening timer ticks +2 immediately. enumerate
subtitle: The last high road that survives the spring thaws.

title: Tithe-Collector's Runner
body:
His tally-rod has notches from a dozen villages. The villages are now empty. He collects for the Margravine. She does not ask where the grain goes.

**Debt they owe:** He owes his soul to the Margravine's ledger. If you give him a name from the list, he will mark it paid — but the ghost of that name will haunt you.

**Price of aid:** 1 Supply or a story about a tax collector who died hungry.
subtitle: Tally-rod, empty stomach, and a list of names.

title: Roadside Prior
body:
The relic is a finger bone. The prior claims it belonged to a saint who starved to death. The saint was an Utaran missionary. The Acasians ate his offerings.

**Debt they owe:** The prior's order swore to feed the poor. They have failed. He will help anyone who shares a meal.

**Price of aid:** A crust of bread and a prayer. If you refuse, the relic's ghost will follow you (--1 die on all stealth rolls for one scene).
subtitle: Three lay brothers guarding a relic.

title: Hedge-Witch
body:
Her price is a story. The story must have a bad ending. She has heard all the good ones. The bridges listen when she speaks.

**Debt they owe:** She once cursed a tax collector. The curse still echoes. If you help her lift it, she will teach you a route that ignores the Curse once.

**Price of aid:** A story that ends with a death. If the story is true, she gives you a Salt Ward (Diamond). If false, the bridges will remember you.
subtitle: Knows which bridges eat travelers.

title: Free Company Captain
body:
He has served three kings this year. He does not remember their names. His first contract was with a man who called himself emperor. The man is dead. The contract is not.

**Debt they owe:** He owes back pay to his company. If you pay 1 Supply, he will fight for you for one scene.

**Price of aid:** A contract signed in blood. If you break it, the Curse Awakening ticks +2.
subtitle: Pike and shot between contracts.

title: River Reeve
body:
His paper is a single page folded into a boat. The other half is elsewhere. The other half is in the Margravine's counting house. She does not know.

**Debt they owe:** He stole the half-page from the Margravine. If you return it, he will waive all tolls for a season.

**Price of aid:** A bribe of 1 Boon or a secret about the river. He will also betray you for a better offer.
subtitle: Rents every boat twice.

title: Salt-Baron
body:
His salt is gray. It was cut with ashes from a burned village. The village refused to pay the imperial salt tax. The empire is dead. The salt is not.

**Debt they owe:** He took a loan from the Margravine's counting house. If you pay it (2 Supply), he will give you a Salt Charter (pass any ford free).

**Price of aid:** A wagon of gray salt. Using it in a bargain gives +1 die to intimidation, but the ghost of the burned village will haunt the transaction.
subtitle: Hired blades; owns the ford and your timetable.

title: Blackwood Matriarch
body:
Her garden grows tombstones. She waters them with tears—her enemies'. Her grandmother was the last Acasian to hold an imperial title. The empire took it back. She has not forgotten.

**Debt they owe:** The empire stole her grandmother's title. If you recover the original charter (in the Sealed Dowry Chest), she will name you her heir.

**Price of aid:** A lock of hair from a blood enemy. She will not say whose.
subtitle: Tends the feud like a garden.

title: Ex-Imperial Surveyor
body:
The map shows villages that no longer exist. The surveyor visits them anyway. She leaves offerings of bread and ink. The ghosts do not eat. They watch.

**Debt they owe:** She lost the map's key — a brass compass. Find it, and she will draw you a route that ignores the Curse for one journey.

**Price of aid:** A true name of a dead village. She will trade a secret for it.
subtitle: Has the last accurate map.

title: “King” of Three Villages
body:
His crown was a plowshare. He reversed the curse. The curse reversed back. He does not know.

**Debt they owe:** He borrowed the plowshare from a hedge-witch. The witch wants it back. Return it, and he will grant you a tax waiver.

**Price of aid:** A day's labor in his fields. If you refuse, he accuses you of oath-breaking — start a Feud Spark [4].
subtitle: Iron-nail crown, iron-will taxes.

title: Bride with No Dowry but a Claim J
body:
The claim is to a bridge that drowned. The bride intends to collect. The bridge was built by the legions. The legions are gone. The bridge is not.

**Debt they owe:** Her dowry was the bridge's toll. The Margravine seized it. If you help her collect, she will give you a Bridge Token (Diamond).

**Price of aid:** A dagger from her chest. Using it in a duel gives +1 die, but the bridge's ghost will claim the loser.
subtitle: Daggers in the wedding chest.

title: Margravine of the Broken March Q
body:
She has never lost a feud. Her tally stick is her sword. Her great-great-grandfather was the last imperial governor's clerk. He stole the seal. She still has it.

**Debt they owe:** She is losing her grip on the province. If you settle a feud for her, she will give you a Blood-Peace Charter (Diamond).

**Price of aid:** A signature on her tally stick. Signing binds you to her service until the feud is settled.
subtitle: Half saint, half tax roll.

title: The Lame King K
body:
His throne is a sedan chair carried by debtors. They owe him everything. He owes the Margravine a bridge toll. He has not paid. The bridge remembers.

**Debt they owe:** He cannot pay the toll. If you pay it for him (2 Supply), he will name you his heir for a day — you may issue one royal decree.

**Price of aid:** A ride on his throne. The debtors will carry you, but you will owe them a favor in return.
subtitle: Traveling throne; makes law by pointing.

title: The Cursed Child of Silkstrand A
body:
She is said to be twelve years old. She has been twelve for a century. She was born on the day the last imperial governor died. She does not age. She does not forget.

**Debt they owe:** She is the Curse's accountant. If you find her, she will tell you how many bridges you owe.

**Price of aid:** A name you have never spoken. She will write it in her ledger. The Curse will remember it forever. enumerate
subtitle: A rumor more than a person; her laughter ends sieges.

title: Peat-Fog
body:
The name is not yours. Answer it, and the fog will take you. The fog is the empire's last breath.

**Mechanical hook:** Navigation rolls are Desperate for the scene. On a Miss, a ghostly tax collector appears. It demands a story or a memory. Refusal ticks Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: All horns sound like someone calling your name.

title: Sudden Levy
body:
The levy master has a list. Your name is on it—in fresh ink. The list was copied from an imperial tax roll. The roll is two hundred years old.

**Mechanical hook:** Pay 1 Supply or serve. Serving forces a Resolve test (DV 4). On failure, you gain the Condition Impressed (--1 die to all actions until you escape). Start a Levy Escape [4] timer.
subtitle: Every traveler is pressed for a day's service.

title: Bridge Feud
body:
The chain was forged from a broken oath. It rattles when liars approach. The oath was sworn to the emperor. The emperor is dead. The chain does not care.

**Mechanical hook:** The chain will only lift if you swear an oath to one of the feuding parties. Swearing ticks Curse Awakening +1 (oaths made on bridges always compound). Refusing forces a fight — treat as a Cap 2 adversary.
subtitle: Rival banners drop the chain on your cart.

title: Grain Blight
body:
The blight has a face. It is the face of a tax collector who died hungry. The collector worked for the empire. The empire did not pay him.

**Mechanical hook:** You may pay double (2 Supply) or refuse. Refusing starts a Village Hunt [4] timer. When full, the villagers attack at night (Cap 3 mob).
subtitle: Doubles the tithe; refusal means torches at night.

title: Scree Slide
body:
The enemy raised the toll yesterday. He was expecting you. The pass was the empire's eastern gate. It still remembers the legions.

**Mechanical hook:** Pay 2 Supply to the enemy or find another way. Searching for another way forces a Wits+Lore roll (DV 5). On a failure, you lose 1 segment of progress and gain a Black Mark with the enemy.
subtitle: Seals the pass; the “safe” detour is owned by your enemy.

title: Wedding Turns Ambush
body:
The bride's veil is a shroud. The groom's ring is a knife. The feud began when the empire divided the valley. The valley has not healed.

**Mechanical hook:** You must choose a side or flee. Choosing a side gives you an ally (Cap 2) but starts a Feud Spiral [6] timer with the other. Fleeing costs 1 Fatigue and ticks Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: You are caught between two bloodlines.

title: Witch's Tithe Night
body:
The lights have voices. They are arguing over who should collect. They are the ghosts of imperial tax collectors. They have not stopped working.

**Mechanical hook:** The ghosts demand a story. If you cannot tell one, they take 1 of your Boons (or 1 Supply). If you have nothing, they take a memory — lose 1 XP (refundable by a quest).
subtitle: Lights move in the woods; owe nothing or else.

title: Pox Sign
body:
The pox is a rumor. The desertion is real. The pox came with the last imperial supply train. The supply train never arrived.

**Mechanical hook:** You must travel alone for the next leg (no assists). Start a Disease Timer [4]. When full, each PC gains 1 Fatigue.
subtitle: On a village gate; your escorts desert you.

title: Condotta Breaks
body:
The new colors are the same as the old colors. The captain just wanted to raise morale. He was hired by the Margravine. He was also hired by the Lame King. He is collecting both salaries.

**Mechanical hook:** The company now fights for your enemy. You may bribe them back (2 Supply) or fight them (Cap 3). Bribing ticks Curse Awakening +1 (broken loyalty compounds).
subtitle: The Free Company flips colors mid-march.

title: Heretic Preacher J
body:
The preacher's text is a tax receipt. He reads it like scripture. The receipt was issued by the empire. It is still valid. No one knows to whom.

**Mechanical hook:** The preacher will grant you safe passage through the riot if you give him a relic (any Diamond). If you refuse, the mob attacks (Cap 2, and you are separated from allies).
subtitle: Sparks a march; toll-gates come down in splinters.

title: Imperial Pretender Q
body:
The pretender's seal is a sunburst. The sunburst is slightly crooked. The seal was stolen from the last governor's tomb. The governor's ghost is following him.

**Mechanical hook:** The pretender offers you a charter (Diamond) if you swear loyalty. Swearing ticks Curse Awakening +2 (the ghost of the governor will remember). Refusing makes him a permanent enemy (start a Pretender's Hunt [6] timer).
subtitle: Arrives; every petty lord changes tabards.

title: River Overruns the Levee K
body:
The river's name is “Debt.” It remembers every unpaid crossing. The empire's engineers built the levees. They calculated the flood levels. They did not calculate the Curse.

**Mechanical hook:** You lose 1 Supply (washed away). If you have no Supply, you lose 1 Boon instead. The GM may also tick Curse Awakening +1 (the river demands interest).
subtitle: The pontoon goes; your rivals don't.

title: The Curse Stirrs A
body:
The crossroads has a signpost. The arms are labeled “Regret,” “Hunger,” “The Same.” The post was planted by the last imperial surveyor. She is still walking.

**Mechanical hook:** Roll on the Curse Stirrs table (see Regional Mood section). The party cannot leave until they pay a toll — a story, a memory, or a name. enumerate
subtitle: No matter the road, you return to the same crossroads.

title: Toll-Exemption Plaque
body:
The plaque is a bronze leaf. Hold it up, and the toll-keeper will spit—but step aside. The leaf was minted by the empire. The empire's mines are closed. The metal is still good.

**Curse cost:** Using the plaque ticks Curse Awakening +1 (the bridge will remember your face). If you use it on a bridge that has already taken a toll, the plaque crumbles and the bridge's ghost follows you for a day.
subtitle: For one bridge .

title: Monastery Letter
body:
The letter is sealed with a wax tear. The monks will honor it—or they will not. The abbot was an imperial clerk. He still follows the old forms.

**Curse cost:** The monks will ask you to pray for the dead. If you refuse, the letter burns and you gain a Black Mark with the monastery. If you pray, clear 1 Fatigue but tick Curse Awakening +1 (the dead listen).
subtitle: For bed and bread on a named road.

title: Wine-Right
body:
The wine is from a vine that grows over a mass grave. It tastes of iron. The grave holds the last imperial garrison. They were paid in promises.

**Curse cost:** Drinking the wine gives +1 die to your next social roll, but the garrison's ghosts will appear in your dreams. The GM gains 1 SB to use on a nightmare complication.
subtitle: On an abandoned terrace; locals will work for shares.

title: Condotta Contract
body:
The contract is written in blood. The blood is from the captain's own finger. The contract was copied from an imperial legionary oath. The words have changed. The weight has not.

**Curse cost:** If the contract is broken, tick Curse Awakening +2. The captain's ghost will demand a new contract — signed in your own blood.
subtitle: A signed pike contract .

title: Tithe-Remission Writ
body:
The writ is stamped with a bell. The bell's clapper is a finger bone. The bell was cast from melted imperial coinage. The coinage was debased. The bell rings true.

**Curse cost:** Using the writ forces the village to work for you, but the bell's ghost will follow you. Every season, you must offer it a story or lose 1 Boon.
subtitle: For a village; they owe you a season's labor.

title: Border-Stone Adjustment
body:
The adjustment is a lie. The truth is that the line was always there. The line was surveyed by the empire's best geometers. They are all dead. Their measurements are not.

**Curse cost:** The ghost of the surveyor will appear and demand you measure the new line with your own feet. Walk it exactly (8 steps) or lose 1 Fatigue and tick Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: Move a line two fields over.

title: Pass-Key Charm
body:
The charm is a knotted cord. Untie it to pass—or to stay. The cord was tied by an imperial courier. The courier's route was swallowed by the Curse. The cord remembers the way.

**Curse cost:** The charm works for one season. After that, the courier's ghost will visit you. He will ask for a message to deliver. If you refuse, the charm becomes a curse — all roads lead back to the same crossing.
subtitle: Recognized by Pale Causeway watchmen.

title: Sealed Dowry Chest
body:
The chest is locked with a riddle. The answer is a name you do not know. The name is the last imperial governor's. He wrote it on the inside. He is the only one who has seen it.

**Curse cost:** Opening the chest ticks Curse Awakening +3. The governor's ghost will appear and offer a bargain: the name in exchange for a service. Refusing means the chest locks forever.
subtitle: Of claims, not coin; certain doors open.

title: Mine-Share
body:
The share is a pickaxe. The commune will lend you a miner—or a grave. The mine was opened by the empire's first surveyors. They found iron. They also found something else. They did not name it.

**Curse cost:** The miner will work for you, but the mine's whispers will follow. Once per session, the GM may ask you to name something you found in the dark. If you lie, the miner dies.
subtitle: In the commune; they fight like they mean it.

title: Blood-Peace Charter J
body:
The charter is a white ribbon. Blood will not be spilled while it flies—but blood will remember. The ribbon was woven by a hedge-witch. She used thread from a tax collector's uniform. The collector is dead. The thread is not.

**Curse cost:** The truce lasts one scene. After that, the feud returns with interest — both sides will demand a wergild from you. Pay 2 Supply or start a Double Feud [6].
subtitle: Suspend a feud long enough to move your wagons.

title: Marriage Proxy Q
body:
The proxy is a wedding veil. The veil was worn by a ghost. The ghost was the Margravine's grandmother. She married an imperial legate. The legate never came home.

**Curse cost:** Using the proxy binds the hill-king to you — but the ghost will appear at your own wedding (or any celebration). She will ask for a dance. Refusing costs 1 Boon and ticks Curse Awakening +1.
subtitle: From the Margravine; bind a hill-king to your cause.

title: The Lame King's Traveling Writ K
body:
The writ is a broken scepter. The Lame King's seal is a footprint. The footprint was pressed into wax by his grandfather. The grandfather was a free company captain. He could not write. He used his boot.

**Curse cost:** The writ works only once. After that, the Lame King will send debtors to collect the scepter. If you refuse, start a King's Hunt [6].
subtitle: Troops must make way .

title: Curse-Redemption Rite A
body:
The rite is a whisper. The whisper is a name you have never spoken. The name is the Curse's. It does not want to be spoken. It does not want to be silent. It wants to be paid.

**Curse cost:** Using the rite clears all Curse Awakening segments for one night. The next morning, the Curse returns with double the segments. You cannot use the rite again in the same province. enumerate
subtitle: For one night, no crossroads can hold you.

title: Salt Pan with Broken Spirit-Cage
body: The cage is empty, but it still rattles at night. Something got out. The salt tastes of iron.
subtitle: A white flat where the air hums.

title: Black Marble Temple
body: The temple has no windows. The Maeri do not need light. The steps are warm, as if a great beast sleeps beneath.
subtitle: Steps stained red; the blood never washes away.

title: The Brass Gate
body: Each buoy contains a bound spirit. They sing the names of those who pass. The ninth buoy is silent.
subtitle: A fortified strait with spirit-buoys that scream when crossed.

title: Veiled Sister's Sanctum
body: The mirage is not an illusion. It is a memory the Sister has stolen. The memory is always from a child.
subtitle: Entrance hidden by a mirage that shows your greatest fear.

title: Galanina Slave Market
body: The auctioneer wears a mask. The mask is made from the face of a debt-seller. The face still moves.
subtitle: A circular pit with cages of brass and bone.

title: Esoti Record Hall
body: The scrolls write themselves. The ink is the blood of erased names. The ninth shelf is empty — reserved for the name that must never be recorded.
subtitle: A long chamber with shelves of silent scrolls.

title: Black Hand Garrison
body: The door has no handle. It opens inward only when a name is whispered. The whisper is never forgotten.
subtitle: A nondescript building with no windows and a single door.

title: Breath-less Cellar
body: The hole leads to a tunnel that leads to a tomb. The tomb is a safe house. The candle never burns lower.
subtitle: A root cellar with a single candle and a hole in the floor.

title: Red Desert's Edge
body: The glass is green. It hums with the memory of the prince's curse. The sound is the same as a brass cage rattling. [J] The Ninth Name Shrine — A ruin where a forbidden name is carved into stone. The stone weeps water. The water tastes of iron and forgotten vows. The name is worn smooth — no one can read it, but everyone fears it. [Q] Spirit-Binding Foundry — A forge where brass cages are made. The forge is heated by a bound fire-spirit. It screams when the bellows pump. The screams are prayers in a dead language. [K] The Hollow Vessel Nursery — An orphanage where children are prepared for possession. The children have no shadows. Their shadows have been sold. The ninth cot is always empty — for the child who will be the Hollow's vessel. [A] Ikasha's Sleeping Chamber — A sealed vault beneath Galanina. Inside, a stone sarcophagus. The stone is warm. She Who Sleeps dreams of freedom. Her dreams leak through the cracks — green glass grows where they touch stone. enumerate
subtitle: Where the fertile land turns to dust and glass.

title: Terrified Baker
body: His son was taken for “reeducation” last year. He does not know if the boy is alive. He is afraid to ask.
subtitle: Kneads dough with shaking hands. He knows which Black Hand guards take bribes and which take only silence. He will sell you bread, but he will not meet your eyes. If the Hand asks, he did not see you. He will weep afterward.

title: Ledger Clerk
body: He has a wife and a daughter. The daughter's name is written on a scrap of paper hidden in his shoe. That is his only insurance.
subtitle: Ink-stained fingers, hollow eyes. Copies erasure orders all day. He knows whose names are on next week's list. He will trade that knowledge for a single assurance that his own name isn't on it — but he cannot be sure you can deliver. He is not brave. He is merely desperate.

title: Black Hand Recruit
body: He has never killed anyone. He does not know if he can.
subtitle: Still has a family. Still flinches when the brand touches his arm. He joined because the mines are a death sentence. He does not know what he will be asked to do next week. He is terrified. He will let you pass if you promise to tell his mother he didn't suffer.

title: Mother at the Well
body: The child's name was Laila. She hums her daughter's lullaby to the rope. The well remembers.
subtitle: Gave her youngest child's name to the Sisters. Not because she is evil. Because the alternative was her whole family being taken. She draws water at dawn when acolytes aren't watching. She will not speak of it. But if you ask about the ninth child, she will weep.

title: Black Hand Veteran
body: She has forgotten the taste of honey. She would like to remember.
subtitle: Has served twenty years. Her hands do not shake. She has seen the Sisters' work up close. She knows there is no escape, only delay. She will not help you escape — but she might sell you a day's head start. The price is a story. The story must be true.

title: Esoti Junior Magistrate
body: The key is a brass finger bone. It fits a lock in the Ninth Ledger's vault. She does not know what it opens.
subtitle: Inherited her post from an uncle who disappeared. She knows the laws are lies. She enforces them anyway because the alternative is the Binding Foundry. She drinks too much and weeps in the archive. She has a key to a vault. She will lend it — for a story about what freedom tastes like.

title: Slave
body: She wears a brass tag with a number. She has memorised the number of every slave in the household. She is waiting for the day the numbers no longer matter.
subtitle: Not a rebel. Not a hero. Just a woman who has learned to be invisible. She knows the secret passages behind the kitchen. She will trade directions for a single piece of news from outside — any news, even bad. She wants to know if her village still exists.

title: Black Hand Officer
body: The paper is his daughter's old schoolwork. The ink is his own blood. He does not know if she can still read.
subtitle: He takes bribes. He looks the other way. He has a daughter in the Sisters' care as a “ward.” He knows she is a hostage. He will let you pass if you carry a letter to her — a letter that says nothing, but is written on paper that smells of home. He is not your ally. He is a man drowning.

title: Veiled Sister
body: She wears a veil of hammered silver. Underneath, her face is smooth — no scars, no wrinkles. She has not aged since she took her vows. [J] The Whisperer (Breath-less cell leader) — She has three names, each for a different jurisdiction. She moves through the catacombs like smoke. She will trust you only after you have broken a small law in her presence — not to prove your courage, but to prove you have something to lose. She writes messages on water. The words vanish, but the Sisters cannot read them. Her reflection is missing. She sold it for a name. [Q] The Black Hand's Shadow — A Hand agent who has stopped sleeping. He sees the Sisters' work in his dreams. He knows he cannot leave. He will not betray his oath — but he might fail to see you, if the price is a single night of dreamless rest. The price is a memory. He will take the happiest one. He carries a brass bell that rings once every hour. It is the only thing that keeps him awake. He has not heard it ring in three days. [K] The Esoti Censor (Desperate) — A high-ranking magistrate who has been ordered to falsify a lineage. If she refuses, her family is erased. If she complies, she knows the truth will outlive her. She will give you the original document — for a promise that her grandson will be told, one day, why his grandmother's name was struck from the rolls. The document is written on human skin. The skin was her own, cut from her thigh when she took office. She has no feeling there anymore. [A] The Veiled Sister (Full) — Malignant divine justice made flesh. She does not threaten. She does not bargain. She states what will happen. She is always correct. She has never been seen eating, sleeping, or blinking. She is not a woman. She is a function of the Veil. There is no complexity here. There is only the weight of a god's attention. (No debt. No price. Only survival.) Her veil is made of gold coins from a dozen dead empires. They do not clink. They weep when she speaks. enumerate
subtitle: She was given to the temple at nine. She does not remember her mother. She believes the Veil protects the empire from something worse. She has never seen a slave beaten — they hide that from novices. She is not evil. She is cultivated. A crack in her certainty may take years to open. You do not have years.

title: Spirit-Dust Storm
body: Navigation DV +1. Mark Fatigue. The voices ask for your name. Do not answer. They already know it.
subtitle: Red sand from the desert carries whispering spirits.

title: Brass Gate Closed
body: The “inspection” is a hunt for a Breath-less agent. The agent is in your party. The gate knows. The gate is patient.
subtitle: The strait is sealed for “inspection.” Delay 2 segments.

title: Bound Spirit Breaks Free
body: The spirit was once a child. It weeps as it fights. Killing it feels like murder. Freeing it feels like surrender.
subtitle: A brass cage cracks. The spirit attacks.

title: The Veil Fails
body: You see the face of someone you wronged. They are asking for an apology. You cannot remember what you did. That is the punishment.
subtitle: For a moment, the Maeri's magic falters. Spirit-visions haunt all.

title: Black Hand Sweep
body: Your papers are in order. The Black Hand does not care. They take you anyway. The order was the trap.
subtitle: A sudden search of the district. Everyone's papers are checked.

title: Esoti Audit
body: The magistrate smiles. “Everyone lies. I just need to know how much.” His quill is already moving.
subtitle: A magistrate demands to see your records. Your records are lies.

title: Spirit-Hound Scent
body: The hounds are invisible. You can hear their breathing, close and wet. Their breath smells of brass and old prayers.
subtitle: A pack of bound hounds is on your trail.

title: Slave Raid
body: The villagers are armed. They have been expecting you. You are the bait. The Sister is not here. She is watching.
subtitle: A Veiled Sister's caravan is taking villagers. You are in the way.

title: Ikasha's Whisper
body: “Free me.” The whisper comes from a crack in the floor. A single green eye looks up. The eye is glass. It blinks. [J] The Ninth Name Spoken — Someone in the party speaks a dead name aloud. The air grows cold. A spirit appears. It wants to know why you called. It does not accept silence as an answer. [Q] Sister's Test — A Veiled Sister offers a deal: betray a Breath-less contact for safety. The offer is genuine. The price is your soul. The Sister watches you decide. She is not in a hurry. She has all of eternity. [K] Mass Haunting — The bound spirits rise as one. The Veil is tearing. The spirits do not attack. They simply ask: “Why did you let this happen?” They do not mean the empire. They mean the children. [A] The Demon's Weight Called — The Kalrantha Amulet glows. A voice whispers: “Speak your desire.” The whisper is your own. You do not remember giving it permission. The amulet is not a prison. It is a magnet. It draws you toward your fate. enumerate
subtitle: In a quiet moment, you hear a voice

title: Slave's True Name
body: The name is written on a scrap of skin. The skin was the slave's own. The letters are still warm.
subtitle: Use it to free a bound person — or bind them further.

title: Spirit-Lamp
body: The lamp burns green. The spirit's face appears in the flame. It is weeping. The tears evaporate into glass.
subtitle: Ask one question of a bound spirit. It cannot lie.

title: Brass Seal
body: The seal is warm. It glows when a Sister is lying. It also glows when you are lying. The Sister does not ask which.
subtitle: Safe passage in a Sister's sanctum for one visit.

title: Veil-Clip
body: The clip is a small brass spider. It crawls onto your collar and whispers. It whispers the names of those who cannot speak.
subtitle: Speak without being silenced by Maeri magic.

title: Erased Name Page
body: The ink is still wet. The name was erased ten minutes ago. The page is warm. It has a pulse.
subtitle: A page from the Esoti record with a name struck through.

title: Breath-less Cipher
body: The cipher is written on a leaf. The leaf dissolves when read. The water remembers. The water does not forgive.
subtitle: A codebook for reading secret messages on water.

title: Spirit-Hound Whistle
body: The whistle is made from a child's bone. The child was the hounds' last victim. The hounds remember her scent.
subtitle: Call off a pack of bound hounds once.

title: Ikasha's Dream
body: The dream arrives as a headache. The vision is clear. The cost is one memory. The memory is always of a door closing.
subtitle: One prophetic vision of the Maeri's next move.

title: Black Hand Mask
body: The mask has no eye holes. The mask sees for you. It also remembers. It will report what it saw to the Hand. [J] Cage-Maker's Flaw — A key that opens any spirit-cage. One use. The key is a bent nail. It was the flaw the cage-maker left. The flaw is also a prayer. The cage-maker does not know to whom. [Q] Drowned Sister's Secret — The location of a hidden Breath-less archive. The archive is in a well. The well is guarded by a ghost. The ghost's name is Mercy. She does not remember why. [K] Ninth Sister's Veil — Wear it to appear as a Veiled Sister for one hour. The veil is also a noose. Do not tie it too tight. The Sister who gave it to you is already dead. She did not untie it. [A] The Unnamed Prince's Map — A map to the original Kalrantha temple. The map is drawn on human skin. The skin was the prince's own. The map glows under moonlight. It shows the way — and the cost. enumerate
subtitle: Wear it to pass as a Hunter for one scene.

title: Inaea (Angel of the Spider)
body: A patron of Mercy & Connection.

title: Carrion King
body: A patron of Decay & Renewal.

title: Ikasha (She Who Sleeps)
body: Ikasha is the hush between footfalls, the patience of dark water, the black-feathered watcher at every threshold. In stillness she gathers what might be, at crossroads she whispers of what may yet come. Ravens circle her, bearing secrets between worlds. Her followers learn to move unseen and speak unremembered, becoming shadows that slip between what is and what could be.
subtitle: The Hush Before the Choice

title: Grimmir (The Wild Speaker)
body: A patron of Seasons & Sacrifice.

title: Palinode (Queen of Encores)
body: Once a road-cantor who swore to reconcile feuding towns with procession and song, Palinode died between feasts with a chorus unfinished. Yet the refrain refused to end: it braided toasts, hymns, work-chants, and tavern rounds into a living current that still coils through markets and moots. Where a crowd leans forward and a maker holds breath, she arrives.
subtitle: Performance & Rapture

title: The Pale Shepherd Guide of Transitions
Kuva The Sky That Takes Many Names
Mykkiel Arbiter of the Covenant
body: Mykkiel is the unwavering judge of covenants, the divine lawgiver whose scales and sword uphold sacred order. He is not good, nor evil – he is the law. Mercy without justice is weakness; justice without law is chaos. His followers are judges, templars, and scribes who enforce divine law with zealous devotion, seeing the world in absolutes of sanctity and transgression.
subtitle: Law & Zeal

title: The Carrion King Lord of Decay and Renewal
body: The Carrion King does not rule. He waits. He is the patience of the forest floor, the hunger of the root, the slow, inevitable turning of flesh to soil. He is not evil—he is necessary. Without decay, there is no growth. Without rot, no renewal. Without the carrion, no feast for the living.

title: Khemesh The Abyssal Maw
body:
Everyone imagines the deep as open. It is the opposite of open.

Go down far enough and the water stops being a place you are in and becomes a thing that is on you — on the chest, on the eyes, on the joints of the fingers — and there is no up, because up is four thousand feet of the same weight, and no direction is a way out. The room does not have walls. The room is *everywhere at once and closing*, and it has been closing since before there were eyes to be shut by it.

Khemesh is that. Not a lord of it. There is no court down there, no throne, nothing that answers, and no gap between him and the condition of being at that depth. What his sworn receive is not a voice but a certainty arriving inside them rather than at them: that everything descends in the end, that the descent is narrow, and that nothing is waiting at the bottom to receive it.

He is Raéyn's son, which the sailors say and the sworn do not discuss. Whatever the sea is when it is wild and enormous and alive, this is what it is at the bottom of itself, in the dark, with the lid on.

You will know a marked one before they speak. Shadows hang against them wrong, heavy, like wet cloth. They flinch at sounds nobody else has heard. They stand nearer to walls than they used to. And they are calm about it — that is the part that empties a room — calm the way a man is calm after the argument is over and he has lost it.
subtitle: Where Sound Cannot Follow

title: Oya The Wind of the Sahel
body: Oya is the harmattan — the dry wind that sweeps the grasslands, carrying red dust from the Ashaani desert. She is neither cruel nor kind. She is the breath that clears the old, the storm that scatters what has grown stagnant, the wind that opens a locked door by rattling it until the latch gives way.
subtitle: Liberation & Dust
