Lucky Jack The Lord of Thieves
body: Lucky Jack was once a mortal — a thief so skilled that even the gods took notice. He stole a coin from the Hollow's own pocket, and the Hollow laughed. 'You are clever,' it said. 'But cleverness is a debt. One day, I will collect.' Jack has been collecting luck ever since. He is the Unspent Coin, the Magpie King, the patron of urchins, beggars, and thieves who plan their work and work their plan. His followers are not murderers — they are professionals. They know that the greatest heist is the one that leaves no trace, no victims, and no debts. Yet every stroke of luck is a loan, and Jack's interest rates are legendary. When he comes to collect, you will wish you had never met him.
subtitle: Luck & The Heist

title: The Unbroken Way The Way of Balance
Ibeji The Twin Stones
body: Ibeji are twin spirits — one of stone, one of gear — who dance together to keep the walking cities of Ngomebe alive. They were not born; they were carved. The first stone city needed a keystone and a bearing, and the first Mason-Kin and the first Aeler vent-prior worked together for nine years to make them fit. When the city walked, the two spirits emerged from the joint — one from the stone, one from the gear — still holding hands. They teach that no craft is complete without another, that a bridge needs two shores, and that the strongest keystone is the one that bears the weight of a partner's trust.
subtitle: Two Hands Beneath One Weight

title: Lunara The Silver Quiet
body: Lunara walks where torchlight falters: crossroads, tidal edges, shadowed sanctuaries. She is the whisper beneath silver skies, a torch-bearing guide to mysteries that lie between waking and dream. The ancients know her as triple-formed: maiden of new light, mother of full radiance, crone of waning shadow. Her gifts are gentle yet perilous: a mirror that reveals as much of the seeker as the sought, a key that opens ways better left closed, a light that makes the unseen plain. Her sigil is the silver spiral, etched in water, mirror, or stone.
subtitle: Moon & Mystery

title: Mor'iraath The Destroyer
body: Mor'iraath is the demon of absolute destruction—not the slow decay of rot, nor the patient erosion of water, but the joyful, all-consuming fire that reduces everything to ash and memory. He delights not in the process of ruination, but in the perfect moment of combustion, when something that was becomes something that never will be again. His followers become agents of finality, wielding flame that leaves no trace, no remains, and no possibility of reconstruction. To serve him is to embrace the beauty of endings and the power that comes from making things never have been. Where Malachai corrupts and Khemesh crushes, Mor'iraath ignites.
subtitle: Annihilation & Inferno

title: Longhouse Quarter
body: The forum's marble floor is worn smooth by dancing feet, not sandals. The ghosts of tax collectors weep in the corners.

title: Milefort XVII
body: Earth bank, stone gate; faded eagle over fresh knotwork. The eagle's stone wings were reglued after a lightning strike. It still leans left — toward the steppe.

title: Stone Ford
body: Plank-palings and a customs table at knee-height; border as bureaucracy. The ford changes hands every season. The customs table never moves. The wood is stained with ink and blood.

title: Villa Granary
body: Barracks with a tile roof; spear racks where olives once slept. The olive press still works. The pressers are now armorers. The oil is for lamps, not cooking.

title: Twin Court
body: Mallus ring beneath an oak, basilica bench across the lane. The oak and the bench are the same distance from the well. The well is neutral ground. The well has a chain.

title: Blackwood Road
body: Milestones re-carved in runes and Utaran both. The runes say “safe passage.” The Utaran says “toll payable twice.” The third line is scratched out.

title: Burial Field
body: Ship-ridge mounds beside tiled mausolea, both garlanded. The mausolea have fresh offerings. The ancestors are not picky. The ship-mounds whisper at dawn.

title: Hill Amphitheater
body: A lord's hall raised in an old arena's curve; power in architecture. The lord's throne is a gladiator's chair. He does not know who last sat in it. The sand beneath is still dark.

title: New Raivon
body: March capital; grid-streets colliding with wandering lanes. The grid was laid by a surveyor who never came back. The lanes are older. They move at night.

title: Dux's Palace
body: Purple awnings, wolf-hides, law tablets on the wall. The tablets list every treaty broken. The wolf-hides are from the treaty-breakers. They still growl.

title: Hearth-Mother Vesna
body: Keeper of guest-right. She has never lost a quarrel; her voice is soft, her memory longer than the Foedus Stone. She remembers obligations that are not yet owed—and the stone is forgetting, shrinking.

title: March Notary Theodora
body: Utaran-trained legalist. Her left hand writes Utaran, her right writes runes. She signs with her foot. A “third hand” writes in ink that no one can read—not even her. The document is always binding—until the stone forgets.

title: Horse-Reeve
body: Rations pasture between plows and warbands. He measures grass in fistfuls. The Ykrul respect his arithmetic. The Ecktorians pretend not to notice. He is saving fistfuls to patch the stone.

title: Ykrul Envoy
body: Riding under safe-conduct; speaks obligations in proverbs. He never carries a weapon. His tongue is sharp enough. His hostage string has nine knots. He is running out of space—and the stone is running out of memory.

title: Old Legionary
body: Drill-master for Vilikari levies; Utar in muscle memory. He still marks time in paces. The recruits call him “Grandfather Eagle.” The eagle on his shield is chipped. He says the stone's cracks are just more places to put his thumb.

title: Ecktorial Factor
body: Vilikari blood, Ecktorial coin; flows where the market points. His coat has two collars—one for each loyalty. He wears whichever is warmer. His tally has three columns. The third column is labeled “crack width.”

title: Kahfagian Pilot
body: Lantern-law chit and clan tattoo; sea-law on land. He navigates by stars and tariffs. Both change with the season. He has never been lost—only delayed. The stone's cracks are good for smuggling.

title: Marcher-Lord
body: Iron-nail crown, Vilikari law in pocket; a frontier king. His crown was a plowshare. He reversed the curse. His hands are still calloused. He does not sit on his throne. He spends his days pressing his ear to the stone.

title: Queen of Marches
body: Consort-regent; smiles like precedent. She married the Federate King for peace. She kept the kingdom for herself. Her seal is a broken arrow. She keeps a piece of the stone in her pocket—it gets smaller every year.

title: Federate King Aldric
body: Rex-Dux sworn to forms, sung by his own. He has three thrones—oak, marble, and saddle. He uses whichever is not being argued over. Lately, all three are dusty. He has stopped arguing. He just listens to the stone.

title: Elder of Elders
body: Thing-council speaker; a nod can unmake a clan. He speaks once a year. The rest of the time he listens—and remembers. But his memory is cracking like the stone. He has started writing things on his own skin.

title: Law Tangle
body: Mallus verdict vs. basilica writ — whose seal bites? The oak judge and the marble judge are cousins. They send each other holiday cards. The case has been open for three generations. The stone has forgotten who started it.

title: Foedus Seal
body: Settlement and stipends confirmed for a season. The seal is a bronze wolf's head. It warms when the treaty holds—and cools when it doesn't. The wolf's eyes are garnets. One eye is cracked.

title: Mallus Right
body: Hold court under the oak and be obeyed. The oak is older than the kingdom. Its roots have seen more verdicts than the throne. The acorns are bitter. The oak's leaves are falling early.

title: Stipend Arrears
body: Paid in salt and grain; portable, persuasive. The salt is gray. The grain is from last harvest. Both are worth more than coin. The soldiers will accept. The stone will not.

title: Utaran Patent
body: Citizenship-style privilege; doors open, bows deepen. The patent is a worn scrap of vellum. It has been folded and refolded for a century. The seal is a sunburst. The sunburst is fading.

title: Stall-Right
body: Customs favor on a frontier market line. The stall is a painted plank. Plant it, and the tax man will pretend not to see you. He will remember the favor. The stone will not.

title: Remount Allotment
body: Fresh horses from royal paddocks, no questions. The horses are from the king's own herd. They know the roads better than you. They also know the king's secrets. They refuse to cross the stone's shadow.

title: Bridge Farm
body: Imperial for a season; funds and friends accrue. The bridge toll is a copper a head. The bridge keeper is your new best friend. He also keeps a list of your enemies. He scratches the list on the stone.

title: Purple Warrant
body: Wear the stripe; officials defer on sight. The stripe is a sash. It was a curtain in a past life. The present life is yours. Do not lose it. The stone's crack has swallowed one like it.

title: Queen's Audience
body: Private; a whisper becomes policy. The audience is held in a garden. The flowers are listening. The gardener is a spy. The gardener is also the queen. She keeps a piece of the stone under her tongue.

title: Dux Commission
body: Command a mixed unit with pay authority. The commission is a baton. It doubles as a mace in a pinch. It also doubles as a receipt. The receipt is overdue. The stone has a receipt for the stone.

title: Wolf Milepost
body: Stacked stones; wind whines through eye-holes. Each stone is a tally. Remove one, and the wind names you debtor.

title: Remount Station
body: Low corral with stamped snow and tether-posts. The tether-posts are carved with the names of dead horses. The living ones remember.

title: Birch Windbreak
body: Above black-earth tracks; old offerings in the bark. The offerings are strips of wool. Each strip is a prayer for safe crossing.

title: Salt Pan
body: Crusted white; hoof-prints like stars across the void. The pan has a name: “The Khagan's Mirror.” Look into it, and you see what you owe.

title: Reed Ford
body: River braids; poles mark yesterday's safe line. The poles shift in the night. The river's path changes with the moon.

title: Trading Palisade
body: Way-post with wolf-skull pennons snapping. The skulls face outward. They watch for liars and bad weights.

title: Winter Camp
body: Felt tents in a horseshoe facing the wind. The open end is for guests. The closed end is for the ancestors.

title: Kurgan Field
body: Low barrows; horse-bones bead the grass like prayer beads. The bones were placed by a bone-singer. Each bead is a name.

title: Watch Kopje
body: Lonely tor with signal fire-scar; the eye of the steppe. The fire-scar is from a signal that saved a host. The smoke still smells of hope.

title: Pontoon Crossing
body: Laced hides creak; the current speaks fast and hungry. The hides are from horses that died crossing. Their ghosts still pull.

title: Council Hollow
body: Standards planted; the ground tamped like a war-drum. The standards have ears. Speak a treason here, and every clan will know by dawn.

title: Khagan's Station
body: Broad ger on a timber platform; guards in silence. The guards never blink. They are paid in salt and secrets.

title: Sky Steppe
body: Open, wind like a voice; tracks keep pace beside you. The tracks are not yours. They belong to the ancestors who ride with you.

title: Herd-Scout
body: Three ponies and six opinions; the horizon as a map. He can read a trail by the way the grass bends. He can read a liar by the way a rider checks his exits.

title: Camp-Mother
body: Chooses where fires live; hospitality is law. She has never drawn a blade. She has never needed to.

title: Banner Youth
body: Minding the wolves' tooth standard; pride as duty. The standard is older than his grandmother's grandmother. He will die before it falls.

title: Salt-Broker
body: Weighs promises like grain; trade as precision. Her scales are honest—because a dishonest scale is a broken tool, and tools are expensive.

title: Remount Keeper
body: String-master with a book of brands; horses as currency. His book is written in hoof-prints. He can read a horse's soul.

title: Bone-Singer
body: Knows the kurgans' proper names; death as memory. She sings the names of the dead each dawn. The dead sing back.

title: Road-Judge
body: Tümen scribe with seals and a patient ear. His seals are from three empires. He uses whichever one is still valid.

title: Noyan Envoy
body: Silver paiza, iron smile; diplomacy as a blade. His paiza was a gift from a Khagan who is now dead. He does not mention that.

title: Host Captain
body: The tent-wall is a map; strategy in every fold. He can see a battle in the way smoke rises. He is usually right.

title: Falcon Courier
body: Leather gauntlets, answers sooner than asked. The falcon is a sleeper agent. It belongs to a different clan. The courier doesn't know.

title: Khatun of Ring
body: Keeper of camp-law and hostage strings. Her strings are braided from the hair of hostages. She knows each strand's owner.

title: Khagan's Kin
body: A nephew or niece sent to bind a foedus with a look. They have never lost a negotiation. They have never needed to speak.

title: Sky-Speaker
body: Shaman of storms; shortcuts owe them a price. They can call lightning—or call it off. The price is always a story.

title: White Squall
body: Dry snow, lost horizons; navigation by gut and horse sense. The snow tastes of iron. Someone is bleeding nearby.

title: Rasputitsa
body: The road becomes porridge; wheels are lies on the earth. The mud has a smell—old blood and older lies.

title: Remount Sickness
body: A cough in the string; swaps get awkward, trust thinner. The cough is a curse. The horses know who cast it.

title: Salt Shortage
body: Meat spoils; tempers thin like winter air. The salt was cut with grave dust. Someone wanted the winter to be hard.

title: Hostage Call
body: Protocol invoked; someone must sit in the tent. The tent has no floor. The hostage can see the earth beneath—and the bones.

title: Feud Spark
body: A name spoken wrong reopens an old debt; blood is the only coin that pays. The name was spelled correctly. The insult was in the pause before it.

title: Grassfire
body: Runs with the wind faster than horses; escape as a prayer. The fire has a face. It is the face of a Khagan who burned a village.

title: Foedus Recall
body: Treaty terms re-read; your papers disagree. The treaty was written on both sides. The other side used a different ink.

title: River Break
body: Ice goes; ferries don't; crossing becomes a gamble. The ice is still thick in the middle. The edges are lying.

title: Raid Shadow
body: Another banner follows at a patient distance. They are not attacking. They are waiting for you to make a mistake.

title: Kurultai Call
body: Camps converge; travel becomes politics. The kurultai has a list of grievances. Your name is near the top.

title: Wolf Muster
body: A levy raised; every road a checkpoint, every rider a judge. The muster horn is a wolf's skull. It sounds like a scream.

title: Sky Omen
body: Three suns, or none; routes rewrite themselves. The omen is a wedge of cranes flying north in winter. The sky is wrong.

title: Camp Token
body: One night's lawful fire and fodder; hospitality as a right. The token is a horsehair braid. Burn it to claim your fire.

title: Salt Allotment
body: Draw from a named store without quarrel. The allotment is a salt-cake. Break it in half to share.

title: Ford-Right
body: Cross a named braid at lawful depth. The right is a pole. Plant it in the river, and the ford will hold—once.

title: Remount Chit
body: Swap two tired mounts for fresh. The chit is a horse's tooth. The remount keeper will not smile when you present it.

title: Escort Braid
body: Two riders see you through a bad stretch. The braid is woven from the riders' own hair. They will die before they cut it.

title: Safe-Hostage
body: Place or take token-kin for a truce. The hostage is a child. The child is patient.

title: Paiza Tablet
body: Priority on the Wolf Road and at posts. The tablet is bronze. It is warm when your reputation is good.

title: Market-Green
body: Trade under a banner; weapons sheathed. The banner is a green field. No blood may be spilled beneath it.

title: Standard Guard
body: Travel under wolf-tooth; raiders defer. The standard is a wolf's tooth on a pole. Raiders will bow—or die.

title: Ring Audience
body: The Khatun hears you alone; precedent sticks. The audience is held at midnight. The fire is the only witness.

title: Khagan's Writ
body: Doors open, mouths close across the steppe. The writ is a sheet of hammered silver. It bends, but it does not break.

title: Sky's Exception
body: Once, the weather ignores you (storm, whiteout, dust). The exception is a single breath. Use it well.
